mainTopic: The opening משנה of גיטין: when a שליח bringing a גט must declare בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם, where the borders of ארץ ישראל lie for this law, and the גמרא's question about the reason for the declaration
overview: This amud opens מסכת גיטין. The משנה teaches that a שליח who brings a גט from מדינת הים (outside ארץ ישראל) must say, 'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence.' Several תנאים then argue about how far this rule reaches. רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר extend it to places close to ארץ ישראל. The חכמים limit it to bringing a גט from outside or taking one out, and moving one between countries outside ארץ ישראל. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל extends it even to moving a גט between districts. רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר then argue over where the borders lie, especially about עכו. The משנה ends by ruling that inside ארץ ישראל no declaration is needed, and a challenged גט is confirmed through its witnesses' signatures. The גמרא then asks why the declaration is needed at all, and רבה's answer begins on the next amud.

steps.title: A messenger bringing a divorce document from abroad must make a declaration
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion in the משנה: a שליח who brings a גט from מדינת הים must say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who brings a גט from a country overseas must say: 'It was written in front of me, and it was signed in front of me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states its basic rule. A שליח delivering a גט from outside ארץ ישראל must say a specific sentence when he hands it to the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule covers a specific case: a גט coming from מדינת הים, which means outside ארץ ישראל. The required sentence has two parts: the שליח saw it being written, and he saw it being signed. The משנה does not give a reason here, and the rest of the משנה argues about how far the rule reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: A divorce document
Literally 'country of the sea'; any place outside ארץ ישראל
The one who brings; here, the agent carrying the גט
'It was written in my presence and signed in my presence'; the required declaration

steps.whyThisMatters: This declaration is the subject of the whole first פרק. Every opinion that follows is arguing about where this one rule applies.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה only tells you what the שליח must say. It does not give a reason, so don't guess the reason yet. The גמרא asks about it in step 10.

phrases.english: One who brings a bill of divorce from a country overseas,
phrases.notes: 'Overseas' here simply means anywhere outside ארץ ישראל, even if no sea is crossed.

phrases.english: is required to say:
In my presence it was written, and in my presence it was signed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם, צָרִיךְ שֶׁיֹּאמַר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליח bringing a גט from outside ארץ ישראל must declare בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל extends the rule to רקם and חגר
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says the declaration is required even when bringing a גט from רקם or from חגר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל says: Even someone who brings a גט from רקם or from חגר must say it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל adds two more places to the rule. Bringing a גט from רקם or חגר also requires the declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אף ('even') shows he agrees with the first rule and adds cases to it. רקם and חגר are on the edge of ארץ ישראל. So he widens the rule beyond places that are clearly far away.

keyTerms.meaning: Even / also; it adds to the earlier rule
A place on the border of ארץ ישראל
Another place on the border of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says: Even one who brings
from Rekem and from Cheger.
phrases.notes: He means a גט brought from these places must also come with the same declaration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the scope of the first rule to border places
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The declaration is also required when bringing a גט from רקם or חגר.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר extends the rule even to the short trip from כפר לודים to לוד
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says the declaration is required even for a גט brought from כפר לודים to לוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: Even someone who brings a גט from the village of לודים to לוד must say it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר widens the rule even more than רבן גמליאל did. Even a short trip from כפר לודים to לוד requires the declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אפילו ('even') signals that this is the most surprising case so far. לוד is a city in ארץ ישראל, and כפר לודים is close by. Still, רבי אליעזר treats bringing a גט between them like bringing it from outside.

keyTerms.meaning: Even; it introduces a more extreme case
The village of לודים, near לוד
A city in ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: Even
from the village of Ludim to Lod.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ מִכְּפַר לוּדִּים לְלוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the rule further than רבן גמליאל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The declaration is required even when bringing a גט from כפר לודים to לוד.

steps.title: The חכמים limit the rule to overseas, but include taking a document out and moving it between overseas countries
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the declaration is needed only for a גט crossing between מדינת הים and ארץ ישראל in either direction, and for a גט moved from one country to another outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: The declaration is needed only by someone who brings a גט from overseas or takes one there. Also, someone who brings a גט from one country to another country overseas must say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים respond to the wider opinions. They limit the rule to מדינת הים, but they list three cases where it does apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אינו צריך ... אלא ('only') rejects the extensions of רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר. The חכמים add המוליך, a גט taken from ארץ ישראל out to מדינת הים, which the first line did not mention. They also add a גט moved between two countries that are both outside ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages; the majority opinion
Only / except; it limits the rule
The one who takes; carrying a גט out from ארץ ישראל
From one country to another

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, the declaration applies in three cases: bringing a גט into ארץ ישראל, taking one out, and moving one between countries outside ארץ ישראל. It does not apply to places on the edge of ארץ ישראל.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read אינו צריך as 'he never needs to say it.' Combined with אלא, it means 'he needs to say it ONLY in these cases.'

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: One is not required to say
'In my presence it was written and in my presence it was signed,'
except one who brings from a country overseas, and one who takes it there.
And one who brings from country to country within the overseas countries
is required to say: 'In my presence it was written and in my presence it was signed.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the wider opinions of רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר, while adding new cases of its own
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The declaration is required only for a גט brought from or taken to מדינת הים, or moved between countries within מדינת הים.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל extends the rule to moving between districts
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the declaration is needed even when a גט moves from one הגמוניא (district) to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Even from one district to another district.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל builds on the חכמים' case of moving between countries. He says even moving a גט between districts requires the declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים required the declaration between whole countries overseas. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל goes to a smaller unit, the district. So even a smaller move counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A district, a region ruled by a local governor

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even from district to district.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ מֵהֶגְמוֹנְיָא לְהֶגְמוֹנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the חכמים' 'country to country' case down to the district level
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The declaration is required even for a גט moved from one district to another.

steps.title: רבי יהודה marks the borders: רקם, אשקלון and עכו count as outside
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה defines the eastern, southern and northern borders of ארץ ישראל for this law, and says רקם, אשקלון and עכו themselves count as outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: From רקם eastward, and רקם itself counts as the east. From אשקלון southward, and אשקלון itself counts as the south. From עכו northward, and עכו itself counts as the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now defines where 'outside ארץ ישראל' begins. רבי יהודה gives three border cities and says each city itself is on the outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each border has two parts: the area beyond the city is outside, and the city itself (כמזרח, כדרום, כצפון) is also treated as outside. So a גט from these border cities needs the declaration.

keyTerms.meaning: East
South
North
A city on the southern border
A city on the northern border

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: From Rekem eastward,
phrases.notes: He means this area counts as overseas for this law.

phrases.english: and Rekem is like the east;
from Ashkelon southward,
and Ashkelon is like the south;
from Akko northward,
and Akko is like the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from 'which trips need the declaration' to 'where exactly the border lies'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Beyond רקם, אשקלון and עכו is outside ארץ ישראל, and these three cities themselves also count as outside.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: עכו counts as inside ארץ ישראל for divorce documents
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר disagrees with רבי יהודה about עכו and says that for גיטין it counts as ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: עכו is like ארץ ישראל for the laws of גיטין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר argues with רבי יהודה about one city, עכו. For גיטין he says it counts as inside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה had treated עכו as outside, part of the north. רבי מאיר places it inside, so a גט brought from עכו would not need the declaration. The word לגיטין limits his statement to divorce documents only.

keyTerms.meaning: Like ארץ ישראל; it counts as inside the land
For the laws of divorce documents

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two arguments: how far the declaration rule reaches (רבן גמליאל, רבי אליעזר, the חכמים, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל), and where the borders of ארץ ישראל are (רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר, who argue about עכו).
steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not saying עכו is part of ארץ ישראל for every law. The word לגיטין limits his statement to divorce documents.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: עַכּוֹ – כְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְגִיטִּין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: Akko is like Eretz Yisrael with regard to bills of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: עַכּוֹ – כְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְגִיטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה's ruling about עכו
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For גיטין, עכו is treated as inside ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Inside the Land, no declaration is needed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a שליח bringing a גט from place to place within ארץ ישראל does not need to say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who brings a גט from one place to another inside ארץ ישראל does not have to say: 'It was written in front of me and it was signed in front of me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of cases. It says that when a גט travels only inside ארץ ישראל, the שליח does not need to make the special declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 2 to 7 argued about which places count as 'outside' and need the declaration. Now the משנה gives the other side of the picture: inside ארץ ישראל, the declaration is simply not required. So the שליח just hands over the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: The Land of Israel, which is the area defined in step 6
He is not required

phrases.english: One who brings a bill of divorce within Eretz Yisrael,
is not required to say:
"It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence."

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ שֶׁיֹּאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's rules about place. After the arguments over where the borders are, it gives the ruling for a גט that travels only inside ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט brought within ארץ ישראל does not need the declaration בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.

steps.title: If the גט is challenged, check the witnesses' signatures
steps.stepSummary: If someone challenges a גט brought within ארץ ישראל, it is confirmed through the signatures of its witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if there are people who challenge it, it should be confirmed through the people who signed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds what to do when someone, such as the husband, claims the גט is not real. Then בית דין confirms it by checking the witnesses' signatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the declaration, the גט is still accepted as valid. But if someone protests, it is treated like any other legal document: its signatures must be confirmed, either by the witnesses themselves or by matching their handwriting.

keyTerms.meaning: People who challenge or protest; here, someone who claims the גט is forged
It should be confirmed or validated
Its signers, meaning the witnesses who signed the גט
The standard process of confirming that the signatures on a document are real

steps.whatToRemember: Inside ארץ ישראל there is no declaration. A challenged גט is confirmed the normal way, through its signatures.

phrases.english: And if there are those who contest it,
it should be ratified through its signatories.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם יֵשׁ עָלָיו עוֹרְרִים, יִתְקַיֵּים בְּחוֹתְמָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further case to step 8: what happens when the גט that came without a declaration is challenged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a גט is challenged, it is validated by confirming the signatures of its witnesses.

steps.title: Why is the declaration needed at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the reason behind the משנה's rule that a שליח from overseas must say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם, and begins to bring רבה's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason? רבה said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why a שליח bringing a גט from overseas must make the declaration. It then introduces רבה, whose answer comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the rule but no reason. The גמרא wants to know what problem the declaration solves. רבה's answer is only introduced here, so this step is setting up the next move.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the אמוראים that explains and examines the משנה
What is the reason?
An אמורא who gives the first explanation of the rule

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'מאי טעמא' does not refer to the last line you just read about ארץ ישראל. It goes back to the first rule of the משנה: why a גט from overseas needs the declaration.
steps.whyThisMatters: The reason the גמרא finds for the declaration will decide all the borderline cases in the משנה, such as which places count as 'overseas'.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: The reason for the very first rule of the משנה: a שליח from overseas must say 'written and signed in my presence'.

phrases.english: Rabba says:
phrases.notes: His actual answer comes in the next section.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה is finished. The גמרא opens its discussion by going back to the משנה's first rule and asking for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason why a שליח who brings a גט from overseas must declare בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet given here. The answer of רבה is introduced and continues in the next section.
